newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian press sees euro within reach.
newsitem.headline: Austrian press sees euro within reach.

text.p: Austrian newspapers said on Tuesday the European Union's compromise deal tying jobs and economic growth to budget stability had brought the single currency nearer.
"The agreement between Germany and France prevented the Amsterdam summit from becoming an embarrassing flop," conservative daily Die Presse wrote.
"We have moved two steps closer to the single currency, albeit in the shadow of a debate on employment."

But in an editorial Die Presse warned that government leaders could not create jobs by decree. Individual states must now begin removing regulatory impediments to job creation while unions had to give up excessive wage demands.

The left-leaning Der Standard sensed a shift in the EU's political priorities. Former European commission president Jacques Delors and some EU member states, including Austria, had long argued that the bloc needed to do more to fight unemployment, it said.

"But their pleas were in vain. Only the spectacular electoral victory of Lionel Jospin's Socialists in France gave these policies impetus...There has been a sea change in European Union politics," it wrote.
